claims.text: At stage-1, OrderServiceTests.cs:49 seeded `new Order { Id = 1, CustomerId = 1, PlacedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow, Status = "new" }` (no items) and it compiled; the empty-items check lived only in PlaceOrderAsync.

At stage-2 the stage-1 initializer line no longer compiles (no accessible parameterless constructor; CustomerId, PlacedAt, Status cannot be set outside Order); the test now writes `new Order(customerId: 1, OneItem(), DateTimeOffset.UtcNow) { Id = 1 }`.
claims.source_hint: verified: dotnet build of DonHang.Domain from git archive stage-2 with the stage-1 line added; stage-2 OrderServiceTests.cs:56

claims.text: At stage-2 Order's public constructor Order(int customerId, List<OrderItem> items, DateTimeOffset placedAt) throws ArgumentException('an order needs at least one item') for an empty list and ArgumentException for any item with Quantity < 1, then sets CustomerId, Items, PlacedAt and Status = "new".
A check in a constructor runs before `new` hands the object to the caller; if it throws, the caller never gets an order.
claims.source_hint: C# docs: Constructors; Exceptions (a throwing constructor does not return an instance)

claims.text: At stage-2 PlaceOrderAsync creates the order with `new Order(customerId, items, DateTimeOffset.UtcNow) { IdempotencyKey = idempotencyKey }`; it has no items.Count check of its own; IdempotencyKey has an init accessor. Id keeps a public setter (test uses { Id = 1 }).
No code outside Order can create an Order that starts without items at stage-2: the only other constructor is private, and CustomerId/PlacedAt/Status/Items setters are private.

ExceptionHandlingMiddleware catches ArgumentException (by type, wherever thrown) and answers 400 with title 'Invalid request' and the exception message as detail; so an empty order still gets 400 with detail 'an order needs at least one item'.
claims.source_hint: stage-2: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs:29-33; C# docs: try-catch (matches by type); Dtos.cs:18 (no validation attribute)

claims.text: When the constructor throws, PlaceOrderAsync stops before AddAsync, notifier.Send and SaveChangesAsync, so nothing is added or saved.
The first constructor message is word for word the one PlaceOrderAsync threw at stage-1 ('an order needs at least one item').
claims.source_hint: git grep 'an order needs at least one item' stage-1 stage-2 -- 'DonHang.*/*.cs'

claims.text: Because every Order created by code starts with items and Status new, Cancel(), Ship() and MarkPaid() check only the status and never whether the order was built correctly.

A check in a method runs only when that method is called, so an object built without items could exist and be saved until then; a check in the constructor runs before `new` hands the object to anyone.

At stage-1 an item with quantity 0 was caught only by the database CHECK and answered 500 (backend.l1.validating-input); at stage-2 the constructor throws ArgumentException for quantity below 1, which the middleware answers with 400.
